title: Activation Functions: Introducing Non-Linearity
description: Explore why non-linearity is vital. Compare Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Leaky ReLU, and Softmax.

slides.title: Why We Need Non-Linearity ⚡
slides.content:
# The Power of Non-Linear Activation

If you stack 100 linear layers together: $f(x) = W_3(W_2(W_1 x + b_1) + b_2) + b_3$, the entire network mathematically collapses into a single linear transformation: $f(x) = W_{combined} x + b_{combined}$!

> 💡 **The Origami Analogy:**
> Linear operations can only stretch, rotate, and shift paper. An activation function allows the network to **fold** the paper, carving out complex decision boundaries in higher dimensions!

slides.title: The Pantheon of Activation Functions 📊
slides.content:
### 1. ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit)
$$\text{ReLU}(z) = \max(0, z)$$
* **Pros:** Computationally ultra-fast; avoids vanishing gradients for positive inputs.
* **Cons:** Dying ReLU problem (neurons getting permanently stuck at 0).

### 2. Leaky ReLU
$$\text{LeakyReLU}(z) = \max(0.01z, z)$$
* Keeps a tiny slope for negative values so gradients can still flow.

### 3. Softmax (Multi-class Output)
$$\text{Softmax}(z_i) = \frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_{j} e^{z_j}}$$
* Normalizes raw logit scores into a valid probability distribution that sums to 1.0.

quizData.question: What is the guaranteed sum of all output probabilities produced by a Softmax layer across all classes?

options.text: Equal to the number of classes

quizData.explanation: By definition, the denominator of the Softmax function normalizes the exponentials such that all class probabilities sum strictly to 1.0.
